reply.english: Yesterday I went to the market.
I was sitting at home.
I saw my aunt by chance.
Yes, I bought a new shirt.

phrases.arabic: أَوَّل مِبَارِح كَان عِنْدِي شُغْل لِحَدّ الْعِشِيَّة
phrases.transliteration: awwal mbeeri7 kaan 3indi shughul la7add el-3ashiyye

reply.english: I stayed up until two o'clock.
Forgive me, some work came up.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: مرحبا نادين، كيفك؟
dialogue.transliteration: marhaba Nadine, kiifik?
dialogue.english: Hi Nadine, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: أهلين هادي، منيحة الحمد لله. وينك كنت مبارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlein Hadi, mnii7a el-7amdulillah. weinak kent mbeeri7?
dialogue.english: Hi Hadi, good, thank God. Where were you yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: كنت بالشغل، كان عندي دوام لحد العشية
dialogue.transliteration: kent besh-shughul, kaan 3indi dawaam la7add el-3ashiyye
dialogue.english: I was at work, I had a shift until the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: يي، دوام طويل! أكلت غدا؟
dialogue.transliteration: yii, dawaam Taweel! akalt ghada?
dialogue.english: Wow, a long shift! Did you eat lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: لأ، ما كان في وقت. أكلت بس بالليل بالبيت
dialogue.transliteration: la2, ma kaan fi wa2et. akalt bas bil-leil bil-beit
dialogue.english: No, there was no time. I only ate at night at home.

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: يا حرام! أنا رحت عالسوق مبارح وشريت كم غرض
dialogue.transliteration: yaa 7araam! ana ru7et 3as-soo2 mbeeri7 w-shreet kam gharaD
dialogue.english: Poor you! I went to the market yesterday and bought a few things.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: شو شريتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: shu shreeti?
dialogue.english: What did you buy?

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: شريت قمصان وشوية خضرة
dialogue.transliteration: shreet 2emSaan w-shwayyet khuDra
dialogue.english: I bought some shirts and a few vegetables.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: طيب، وبعدين شو عملتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb, w-ba3dein shu 3milti?
dialogue.english: OK, and then what did you do?

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: قعدت عند صاحبتي شوي وشربنا قهوة
dialogue.transliteration: 2a3det 3and Saa7bti shwayy w-sherbna 2ahwe
dialogue.english: I sat at my friend's place a bit and we drank coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: كتير حلو. أنا نمت بكير مبارح من التعب
dialogue.transliteration: ktiir 7elo. ana nemet bakiir mbeeri7 men et-ta3ab
dialogue.english: Very nice. I slept early yesterday from the tiredness.

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: خود راحتك اليوم إذا فيك
dialogue.transliteration: khod raa7tak el-yoom iza fiik
dialogue.english: Take it easy today if you can.

response.english: I didn't do anything, I stayed at home.

pair.english: Where were you at seven o'clock yesterday?

response.english: I was still at work.

pair.english: Did you eat something good yesterday?

response.english: Yes, we cooked kibbeh and it was amazing.

pair.english: How was your evening out yesterday?

response.english: It was quiet, I slept early.

lessons.culture: مبارح is the everyday Lebanese word for yesterday, and أول مبارح is the day before; the MSA أمس sounds like the news, not like a chat. Asking شو عملت مبارح؟ is a normal way to open a catch-up over coffee with a friend or neighbor.

exercises.prompt: Your friend asks: "مبارح شو عملت؟". Reply that you went to the market.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA but far too formal for a casual catch-up; مبارح رحت عالسوق is what is actually said.

exercises.tip: مبارح replaces the MSA أمس in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "وين كنت مبارح بالليل؟". Reply that you were at home.

too_formal.feedback: المنزل is a formal written word; Lebanese say البيت in speech.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "_____ كان يوم طويل." Meaning: Yesterday was a long day.

too_formal.feedback: أمس is the MSA word; in spoken Lebanese the word is مبارح.

exercises.tip: مبارح opens the sentence, like "yesterday" in English.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "تعبت كتير مبارح من _____." Meaning: I got very tired from work yesterday.

too_formal.feedback: العمل is correct but bookish; the everyday word for work is الشغل.

exercises.tip: الشغل is the word Lebanese use for work or a job.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "What did you do yesterday?" (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: ماذا فعلت is MSA; in speech you say شو عملت.

exercises.tip: شو replaces ماذا; عملت is "you did".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Why didn't you come yesterday?" (to a woman)

too_formal.feedback: لماذا لم تأتِ is MSA; Lebanese say ليش ما إجيتي.

exercises.tip: To a woman the verb ends in -ي: إجيتي.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I woke up late yesterday"?

too_formal.feedback: استيقظت is MSA; Lebanese say فقت for woke up.

exercises.prompt: What is the everyday Lebanese word for "the day before yesterday"?

too_formal.feedback: أول أمس is MSA; in speech it is أول مبارح.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: We ate at a nice restaurant yesterday.

too_formal.item: تناولنا الطعام في مطعم جميل أمس
too_formal.feedback: تناولنا الطعام is bookish; Lebanese say أكلنا.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: How late did you stay up yesterday?

too_formal.feedback: إلى أي ساعة is MSA; لأيمتى is the everyday way to ask how late.

phrases.arabic: لَمَّا كِنْت زْغِير كِنْت بِحِبّ إِلْعَب بَرَّا
phrases.transliteration: lamma kent zghiir kent bi7ebb il3ab barra

reply.arabic: وَأَنَا كَمَان، كِنَّا نِلْعَب لِحَدّ الْمَغِيب
reply.transliteration: w-ana kamaan, kenna nil3ab la7add el-mghiib
reply.english: Me too, we used to play until sunset.

phrases.english: I grew up in an old neighborhood in Beirut.

reply.english: Where is Karim now?

phrases.arabic: كِلّ صَيْف كِنَّا نْرُوح عِنْد جِدِّي عِالضَّيْعَة

reply.english: The village is so lovely in summer!

phrases.arabic: سِتِّي كَانَت تِحْكِيلِنَا قِصَص قَبْل مَا نْنَام
أَوَّل بِسْكْلِيت كَان عِنْدِي كَان أَحْمَر
كِنْت خَايِف كْتِير مِن الْعِتْمَة وَأَنَا زْغِير
phrases.transliteration: kent khaayef ktiir men el-3atme w-ana zghiir

reply.arabic: أَنَا كَمَان، كِنْت نَام وَالضُّو مَفْتُوح
reply.transliteration: ana kamaan, kent naam w-eD-Dou maftou7
reply.english: Me too, I used to sleep with the light on.

phrases.arabic: كِنَّا نِمْشِي عِالْمَدْرَسَة سَوَا كِلّ يُوم
لَمَّا كِنْت زْغِير كَان حِلْمِي صِير طَيَّار
phrases.transliteration: lamma kent zghiir kaan 7elmi Siir Tayyaar

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: شو يا ماريا، بتذكري لمّا كنا زغار؟
dialogue.transliteration: shu yaa Maria, bet-zakkeri lamma kenna zghaar?
dialogue.english: Hey Maria, do you remember when we were little?

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: أكيد! أنا كبرت بحيّ قديم ببيروت، وكنت حب العب برّا
dialogue.transliteration: akiid! ana kbiret b-7ayy 2adiim b-beirut, w-kent 7ebb il3ab barra
dialogue.english: Of course! I grew up in an old neighborhood in Beirut, and I loved to play outside.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وأنا كان عندي صاحب اسمو جاد، كنا نلعب كورة بالزاروب
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana kaan 3indi Saa7eb ismo Jaad, kenna nil3ab kuura bez-zaaruub
dialogue.english: And I had a friend named Jad, we used to play soccer in the alley.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: ههه، وأنا أول بسكليت كان عندي كان أحمر
dialogue.transliteration: hehe, w-ana awwal biskliit kaan 3indi kaan a7mar
dialogue.english: Haha, and the first bike I had was red.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: كل صيف كنا نروح عند جدي عالضيعة
dialogue.transliteration: kell Seef kenna nrou7 3and jiddi 3aD-Day3a
dialogue.english: Every summer we used to go to my grandfather's in the village.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: يا سلام! وستّي كانت تحكيلنا قصص قبل ما ننام
dialogue.transliteration: yaa salaam! w-setti kenit ti7kiilna 2iSaS 2abel ma nnaam
dialogue.english: Lovely! And my grandmother used to tell us stories before sleeping.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وكنت خايف كتير من العتمة وأنا زغير
dialogue.transliteration: w-kent khaayef ktiir men el-3atme w-ana zghiir
dialogue.english: And I was very afraid of the dark when I was little.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: مش معقول! أنا كمان. وكنا نمشي عالمدرسة سوا كل يوم
dialogue.transliteration: mish ma3quul! ana kamaan. w-kenna nemshi 3al-madrase sawa kell yoom
dialogue.english: No way! Me too. And we used to walk to school together every day.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: وأنا كان حلمي صير طيّارة
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana kaan 7elmi Siir Tayyaara
dialogue.english: And I dreamed of becoming a pilot.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: شو حلوة هالأيام، الله يرجعها
dialogue.transliteration: shu 7elwe hal-2ayyaam, allah yirja3ha
dialogue.english: How lovely those days were, may God bring them back.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.arabic: إي والله، وقتها كانت الدني أبسط بكتير
dialogue.transliteration: ee wallah, wa2ta kenit id-denye absaT b-ktiir
dialogue.english: Yes really, back then life was much simpler.

response.english: I grew up in Beirut in an old neighborhood.

pair.english: What did you play when you were little?

response.english: We used to play soccer in the alley.
Karim, we were together every day.

pair.arabic: شو كنت بدّك تصير وإنت زغير؟
pair.transliteration: shu kent beddak tSiir w-enta zghiir?
pair.english: What did you want to become when you were little?

response.english: I dreamed of becoming a pilot.

lessons.culture: Many Lebanese families spend the summer in the family's village (الضيعة) with the grandparents, and old Beirut neighborhoods are full of narrow alleys called زواريب where children played football. Talking about الأيام الحلوة, the good old days, is a favorite way to bond.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "وين كبرت؟". Reply that you grew up in an old neighborhood in Beirut.

too_formal.item: نشأت في حي قديم في بيروت
too_formal.feedback: نشأت is bookish; Lebanese say كبرت for grew up.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "شو كنتو تلعبوا وإنتو زغار؟". Reply that you used to play soccer in the alley.

too_formal.item: كنا نلعب كرة القدم في الزقاق
too_formal.feedback: كرة القدم and الزقاق are MSA; Beiruti say كورة and زاروب.

exercises.tip: زاروب is the Lebanese word for a narrow alley.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "كل صيف كنا نروح عند جدي _____." Meaning: Every summer we used to go to my grandfather's in the village.

too_formal.feedback: قرية is the MSA word; Lebanese say ضيعة for a village.

exercises.tip: ضيعة = village; عالضيعة = to the village.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "أول _____ كان عندي كان أحمر." Meaning: The first bike I had was red.

too_formal.feedback: دراجة is the MSA word; Lebanese usually say بسكليت.

exercises.tip: بسكليت is the everyday word for a bicycle.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "My grandmother used to tell us stories before sleeping."
exercises.answer: ستي كانت تحكيلنا قصص قبل ما ننام
accepted: ستي كانت تحكيلنا قصص قبل ما ننام
سِتِّي كَانَت تِحْكِيلِنَا قِصَص قَبْل مَا نْنَام

too_formal.item: كانت جدتي تحكي لنا القصص قبل أن ننام
too_formal.feedback: جدتي and قبل أن are formal; Lebanese say ستي and قبل ما.

exercises.tip: ستي = my grandmother, جدي = my grandfather.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "We used to walk to school together every day."
exercises.answer: كنا نمشي عالمدرسة سوا كل يوم
accepted: كنا نمشي عالمدرسة سوا كل يوم
كنا نمشي سوا عالمدرسة كل يوم

too_formal.item: كنا نمشي إلى المدرسة معاً كل يوم
too_formal.feedback: إلى and معاً are formal; say عـ and سوا.

exercises.prompt: Which word is the Lebanese word for "afraid" (masculine)?

too_formal.feedback: خائف is MSA; in speech it is خايف.

exercises.tip: The ئ of MSA becomes ي: خايف.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Back then life was much simpler"?

too_formal.item: في ذلك الوقت كانت الحياة أبسط بكثير
too_formal.feedback: في ذلك الوقت is formal; Lebanese say وقتها.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: When I was young I dreamed of becoming a pilot.
exercises.answer: لَمَّا كِنْت زْغِير كَان حِلْمِي صِير طَيَّار
accepted: لَمَّا كِنْت زْغِير كَان حِلْمِي صِير طَيَّار
lamma kent zghiir kaan 7elmi Siir Tayyaar
لما كنت زغير كان حلمي صير طيار

too_formal.item: عندما كنت صغيراً كنت أحلم أن أصبح طياراً
too_formal.feedback: عندما and أصبح are formal; Lebanese say لمّا and صير.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: I had a friend named Karim.

too_formal.feedback: لدي and صديق are formal; Lebanese say عندي and صاحب.

reply.english: Oh no! Does it still work?
Look well in the bag.
Get well soon! Go to the doctor.
God keep it safe! Put something on it.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير طارق، شو فيك؟ شكلك تعبان
dialogue.transliteration: SabaaH el-khair Taariq, shu fiik? shakl-ak ta3baan
dialogue.english: Good morning Tarek, what's wrong? You look tired.

dialogue.speaker: Tarek
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور، والله يوم أسود مبارح
dialogue.transliteration: SabaaH en-nuur, wallah yoom aswad mbeeri7
dialogue.english: Good morning, honestly it was a terrible day yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: ليش؟ شو صار؟
dialogue.transliteration: leish? shu Saar?
dialogue.english: Why? What happened?

dialogue.speaker: Tarek
dialogue.arabic: تلفوني خرب وضيّعت مفتاح البيت بنفس اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: talifuuni khirib w-Dayya3et miftaa7 el-beit b-nafs el-yoom
dialogue.english: My phone broke and I lost the house key on the same day.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: يي، حرام! وكيف فتحت الباب؟
dialogue.transliteration: yii, 7araam! w-kiif fata7et el-baab?
dialogue.english: Oh no! And how did you open the door?

dialogue.speaker: Tarek
dialogue.arabic: انتظرت أخي لحد ما إجا، وقطعت الكهربا كل الليل
dialogue.transliteration: ntaZaret 2akhi la7add ma ija, w-2aTa3et el-kahraba kell el-leil
dialogue.english: I waited for my brother until he came, and the power went out all night.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: الله يعينك! وهالصبح؟
dialogue.transliteration: allah yi3iinak! w-haS-Sob7?
dialogue.english: God help you! And this morning?

dialogue.speaker: Tarek
dialogue.arabic: نمت زيادة وما سمعت المنبّه، وتأخّرت عالشغل
dialogue.transliteration: nemet zyaade w-ma sme3et el-menabbeh, w-ta2akhkhart 3ash-shughul
dialogue.english: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm, so I was late for work.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك، هيدا بيصير مع الكل
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhemmak, heyda biSiir ma3 el-kell
dialogue.english: Don't worry, it happens to everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Tarek
dialogue.arabic: وبعدين كمان نسيت الجزدان بالبيت
dialogue.transliteration: w-ba3dein kamaan nsiit ej-jezdaan bil-beit
dialogue.english: And then I also forgot my wallet at home.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: ههه، تعا، الغدا عليي اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: hehe, ta3aa, el-ghada 3aleyy el-yoom
dialogue.english: Haha, come on, lunch is on me today.

dialogue.speaker: Tarek
dialogue.arabic: الله يخليكي، يعطيكي العافية
dialogue.transliteration: allah yikhalliiki, ya3Tiiki el-3aafye
dialogue.english: God bless you, thank you.

response.english: My phone broke yesterday.

pair.english: Why were you late for work?

response.english: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.

pair.english: Where did you lose the key?

response.arabic: ما بعرف، دوّرت عليه بكل مطرح
response.english: I don't know, I looked for it everywhere.
It broke down in the middle of the road.

lessons.culture: قطعت الكهربا, the power going off, is a very real part of daily life in Lebanon, so people say it with a shrug and a joke rather than a complaint. When someone tells you about a mishap the usual replies are سلامتك, يي حرام, and الله يعينك.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "شو صار معك؟". Reply that your phone broke yesterday.

too_formal.feedback: تعطل هاتفي is MSA; Lebanese say تلفوني خرب.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "ليش تأخرت؟". Reply that you overslept and did not hear the alarm.

too_formal.feedback: لم أسمع is MSA; Lebanese say ما سمعت.

exercises.tip: ما + past verb makes it negative.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "نسيت الـ_____ بالبيت." Meaning: I forgot my wallet at home.

too_formal.feedback: محفظة is understood but Lebanese say جزدان for a wallet.

exercises.tip: جزدان is the everyday Lebanese word for wallet.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "_____ الكهربا كل الليل." Meaning: The power went out all night.

too_formal.feedback: انقطعت is MSA; Lebanese just say قطعت الكهربا.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I lost the house key."

too_formal.feedback: أضعت and المنزل are formal; say ضيّعت and البيت.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "My bag got lost at the airport."

too_formal.feedback: فقدت حقيبتي is formal; Lebanese say ضاعت شنطتي.

exercises.tip: شنطة = bag, and ضاع = got lost.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I fell on the stairs and hurt my leg"?

too_formal.feedback: سقطت and أصبت رجلي are MSA; Lebanese say وقعت and أذّيت إجري.

exercises.prompt: What do you say when someone tells you they hurt themselves?

too_formal.feedback: أتمنى لك الشفاء is correct but bookish; سلامتك is the everyday wish.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: The car broke down in the middle of the road.

too_formal.feedback: تعطلت and منتصف are formal; say خربت and نص.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: I cut my hand while cooking.

too_formal.feedback: يدي and أثناء الطبخ are formal; say إيدي and وأنا عم بطبخ.

exercises.tip: عم + verb = doing it right now.

reply.english: Wonderful! May God complete it well for him.

phrases.arabic: قَالُولِي إِنَّك عَمّ تِنْقِل عَ بَيْت جْدِيد

reply.arabic: إِي، إِن شَاءَ الْلَّهُ آخِر الشَّهْر
reply.transliteration: ee, in shaa2 allah aakhir esh-shahr
reply.english: Yes, God willing at the end of the month.

phrases.arabic: عَمّ يِقُولُوا إِنُّو مِحَلّ فُلَان سَكَّر
لِسَّا مِش مِتَأَكِّدِين، يِمْكِن بِس إِشَاعَة
مَا رَح تِصَدِّق شُو صَار مِبَارِح بِالْحَيّ
phrases.transliteration: ma ra7 teSSaddi2 shu Saar mbeeri7 bil-7ayy

reply.english: Congratulations! God keep her for you.
A thousand congratulations! God keep him for them.

reply.arabic: وَلَا شِي، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، عَمّ نِمَشِّي حَالِنَا
reply.english: Nothing, thank God, we're getting by.

phrases.arabic: مَا تِقُول لِحَدَّا بِس سْمِعْت إِنِّن رَح يِسَافِرُوا
phrases.transliteration: ma t2ol la-7ada bas sme3et 2innon ra7 ysaafru

phrases.arabic: هَيْدَا كِلُّو حْكِي نَاس، مَا بَعْرِف إِذَا صَحِيح وِلَّا لَأ
phrases.transliteration: heyda kello 7ki naas, ma ba3ref iza Sa7ii7 walla la2

dialogue.speaker: Rita
dialogue.arabic: مرحبا جورج، شو الجديد عندك؟
dialogue.transliteration: marhaba Jorj, shu el-jdiid 3indak?
dialogue.english: Hi George, what's new with you?

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: أهلين ريتا، ولا شي. إنتي شو أخبارك؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlein Riita, wala shi. enti shu akhbaarik?
dialogue.english: Hi Rita, nothing. What's your news?

dialogue.speaker: Rita
dialogue.arabic: في خبر ما رح تصدّقو! سمعت إنّو سامر خطب
dialogue.transliteration: fii khabar ma ra7 teSSaddu! smi3et 2inno Saamer khaTab
dialogue.english: There's news you won't believe! I heard Samer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: عن جدّ؟ مين قلّك هالخبر؟
dialogue.transliteration: 3an jadd? meen 2allik hal-khabar?
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you this news?

dialogue.speaker: Rita
dialogue.arabic: صاحبتي، وقالتلي كمان إنّو محلّ الحلو اللي بالحيّ سكّر
dialogue.transliteration: Saa7bti, w-2aaltilli kamaan 2inno ma7all el-7ilu illi bil-7ayy sakkar
dialogue.english: My friend, and she also told me the sweets shop in the neighborhood closed.

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: لأ ما بصدّق، يمكن بس إشاعة
dialogue.transliteration: la2 ma baSaddi2, yimken bas 2ishaa3a
dialogue.english: No, I don't believe it, it might just be a rumor.

dialogue.speaker: Rita
dialogue.arabic: معك حق، لسّا مش متأكدين. وإختي تجوّزت الشهر اللي فات
dialogue.transliteration: ma3ak 7a2, lissa mish met2akkdiin. w-2ikhti tjawwazet esh-shahr illi faat
dialogue.english: You're right, we're not sure yet. And my sister got married last month.

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: مبروك! ما كنت أعرف. الله يخلّيلكن ياها
dialogue.transliteration: mabruuk! ma kent a3ref. allah yikhalliilkon yaaha
dialogue.english: Congratulations! I didn't know. God keep her for you.

dialogue.speaker: Rita
dialogue.arabic: الله يبارك فيك. وسمعنا إنّو جابوا صبي
dialogue.transliteration: allah ybaarek fiik. w-sme3na 2inno jaabu Sabi
dialogue.english: God bless you. And we heard they had a baby boy.

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: ألف مبروك! ما تقولي لحدا، بس سمعت إنّن رح يسافروا
dialogue.transliteration: alf mabruuk! ma t2uuli la-7ada, bas sme3et 2innon ra7 ysaafru
dialogue.english: A thousand congratulations! Don't tell anyone, but I heard they're going to travel.

dialogue.speaker: George
dialogue.arabic: معك حق، خلينا ننتظر ونشوف
dialogue.transliteration: ma3ik 7a2, khaliina nentiZer w-nshuuf
dialogue.english: You're right, let's wait and see.

response.english: Nothing, thank God.
No, tell me!
The neighbors told me.

pair.english: Is it true that they're getting married?

response.english: I don't know, that's what they're saying.

lessons.culture: Neighbors and relatives in Lebanon share news constantly, and good news is met with مبروك or الله يتمّملو بالخير. Before repeating gossip people often protect themselves with عم يقولوا, they are saying, or ما بعرف إذا صحيح.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "سمعت إنّو سامر خطب". Reply asking who told you this news.

too_formal.feedback: أخبرك is MSA; Lebanese say مين قلّك.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "إختي تجوّزت الشهر اللي فات". Reply with congratulations.

too_formal.feedback: That blessing is correct but formal; مبروك is what is said first.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "_____ إنّو محلّ فلان سكّر." Meaning: They're saying that such-and-such shop closed.

too_formal.feedback: يقال is bookish; Lebanese say عم يقولوا.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "لسّا مش متأكدين، يمكن بس _____." Meaning: We're not sure yet, it might just be a rumor.

too_formal.feedback: شائعة is MSA spelling and sound; Lebanese say إشاعة.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "What's the latest news with you?"

too_formal.feedback: آخر أخبارك is formal; شو الجديد is what people ask.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "You won't believe what happened yesterday in the neighborhood."
exercises.answer: مَا رَح تِصَدِّق شُو صَار مِبَارِح بِالْحَيّ
accepted: مَا رَح تِصَدِّق شُو صَار مِبَارِح بِالْحَيّ
ma ra7 teSSaddi2 shu Saar mbeeri7 bil-7ayy
ما رح تصدق شو صار مبارح بالحي

too_formal.item: لن تصدق ما حدث أمس في الحي
too_formal.feedback: لن and ما حدث are MSA; Lebanese say ما رح and شو صار.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "They told me you're moving to a new house"?
options: قَالُولِي إِنَّك عَمّ تِنْقِل عَ بَيْت جْدِيد
exercises.answer: قَالُولِي إِنَّك عَمّ تِنْقِل عَ بَيْت جْدِيد
accepted: قَالُولِي إِنَّك عَمّ تِنْقِل عَ بَيْت جْدِيد

too_formal.item: أخبروني أنك تنتقل إلى منزل جديد
too_formal.feedback: أخبروني and منزل are formal; say قالولي and بيت.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "a baby boy" in Lebanese?

too_formal.feedback: ولد ذكر is formal; Lebanese say صبي.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: I heard that Samer got engaged.

too_formal.feedback: أن is formal; Lebanese say إنّو.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: That's all just people's talk.

too_formal.feedback: هذا and كلام are MSA; Lebanese say هيدا and حكي.

phrases.arabic: سَافَرْت عَمَدِينِة تَانْيِة الأُسْبُوع اللِّي فَات

reply.english: Praise be to Allah for your safe return.
And how was it? Tasty?
Praise be to Allah that you enjoyed it.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وين كنت يا بلال؟ صرلي جمعة ما شفتك
dialogue.transliteration: ween kent ya Bilaal? Sarli jem3a ma shiftak
dialogue.english: Where have you been, Bilal? I haven't seen you for a week.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: كيف سافرت؟
dialogue.transliteration: keef saafart?
dialogue.english: How did you travel?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: قدّيش أخدت الرحلة؟ المسافة طويلة؟
dialogue.transliteration: 2addeesh akhadet erre7le? elmasaafe Tawiile?
dialogue.english: How long did the journey take? Is it far?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وشو شفت عالطريق؟
dialogue.transliteration: w shu shift 3aTTarii2?
dialogue.english: And what did you see on the way?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: ووين بقيت؟
dialogue.transliteration: w ween b2iit?
dialogue.english: And where did you stay?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وأكلت من أكل البلد؟
dialogue.transliteration: w akalt min akl elbalad?
dialogue.english: And did you eat the food of the country?

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: كتير طيّب! بس الرحلة كانت متعبة
dialogue.transliteration: ktiir Tayyeb! bas erre7le kaanet mut3be
dialogue.english: Very tasty! But the trip was tiring.

response.english: Very nice, praise be to Allah.

pair.english: How long did the trip take?

response.english: Four hours.
In a small hotel.
We arrived after noon.
Yes, praise be to Allah, I arrived safely.

lessons.culture: Lebanon has had no passenger trains for decades, so a train journey is something Lebanese do abroad; at home they travel by car, bus or shared taxi ("سرفيس"). Whoever comes back from a trip is greeted with "الحمد لله على السلامة", said in the same words in every dialect, and then asked for the whole story.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "قدّيش أخدت الرحلة؟" Say four hours.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; in speech a trip "أخدت" so many hours.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "جرّبت الأكل المحلّي؟" Say yes, you tried it (a man speaking).

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "إي" is the spoken "yes" and the ending "ـو" means "it".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "شريت _____ قبلا بيوم." (I bought the ticket the day before.)

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "شريت" and "قبلا بيوم" are the spoken forms.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "نزلت بأوتيل زغير _____ عالبحر." (I stayed in a small hotel near the sea.)

too_formal.feedback: This is the written form; in speech "near" is "قريب عـ".

exercises.tip: "نزلت ب" is how you say you stayed at a hotel.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I took the train from the main station."

too_formal.feedback: Fine words, but read with case endings it is written Arabic; say it plainly.

exercises.tip: Many Lebanese also say "الترين" for the train.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I packed my suitcase the night before."

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "ضبّ" is the Lebanese verb for packing.

exercises.tip: "شنطة" is the everyday word for a suitcase or bag.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "We arrived after noon."

too_formal.feedback: The meaning is right; in Beirut the ظ of "الظهر" is said as ض.

exercises.tip: Lebanese often say ظ as ض or ز.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "The journey took four hours"?
Which sentence means "I came back tired but happy" (a man speaking)?

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "بس" is the spoken "but".

exercises.tip: "تعبانة بس مبسوطة" is what a woman says.

exercises.prompt: Put in order: "الشبّاك / قعدت / حدّ"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "قعدت حدّ" is the spoken "sat next to".

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: "الأسبوع اللي فات / عمدينة تانية / سافرت"
exercises.answer: سافرت عمدينة تانية الأسبوع اللي فات
accepted: سافرت عمدينة تانية الأسبوع اللي فات
سَافَرْت عَمَدِينِة تَانْيِة الأُسْبُوع اللِّي فَات
سافرت على مدينة تانية الأسبوع اللي فات
سافرت عمدينة تانية الجمعة اللي فاتت

too_formal.item: سافرتُ إلى مدينة أخرى الأسبوع الماضي
too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "اللي فات" is the spoken "last".

reply.arabic: خَيْر إِن شَاءَ الله، شُو صَار؟
reply.transliteration: kheir in shaa2 allaah, shu Saar?
reply.english: Good, God willing, what happened?

phrases.arabic: رَح يِجِينَا مَوْلُود جْدِيد إِن شَاءَ الله
phrases.transliteration: ra7 yejiina mawluud jdiid in shaa2 allaah

phrases.arabic: بَيِّي رِجِع مِن المُسْتَشْفَى وَهَلّق مْنِيح
phrases.transliteration: bayyi reje3 min elmustashfa w halla2 mnii7

reply.english: May Allah reward you with good.
I heard it this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Yasser
dialogue.arabic: الله يخلّيك. وفي كمان خبر تاني
dialogue.transliteration: allah ykhalliik. w fi kamaan khabar taani
dialogue.english: Thank you. And there is another piece of news too.

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.arabic: ألف مبروك! كلّ هالأخبار الحلوة سوا؟ شو هالحظّ! وين الحلوينة؟
dialogue.transliteration: alf mabruuk! kell hal2akhbaar el7elwe sawa? shu hal7aZZ! ween el7elwayne?
dialogue.english: Many congratulations! All this good news at once? What luck! Where are the sweets?

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله على سلامته
dialogue.transliteration: il7amdu lillaah 3ala salaamto
dialogue.english: Praise be to Allah for his recovery.

dialogue.speaker: Yasser
dialogue.arabic: فكرة حلوة! بخبّر الكلّ
dialogue.transliteration: fikra 7elwe! bkhabber elkell
dialogue.english: Great idea! I'll tell everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.arabic: مبروك مرّة تانية يا صاحبي، فرحتلك من كلّ قلبي
dialogue.transliteration: mabruuk marra taanye ya Saa7bi, fre7tellak min kell 2albi
dialogue.english: Congratulations again, my friend, I am glad for you with all my heart.

pair.english: I have good news for you.

response.arabic: خَيْر إِن شَاءَ الله، شُو صَار؟
response.transliteration: kheir in shaa2 allaah, shu Saar?
response.english: Good, God willing, what happened?
Congratulations, I am very happy for you.

pair.english: When did you hear the news?

response.english: I heard it this morning.

pair.english: May Allah bless it for you.

response.english: May Allah reward you with good.

response.arabic: إي، الحمد لله، فرصة ما بتتعوّض
response.transliteration: ee, il7amdu lillaah, furSa ma btet3awwaD
response.english: Yes, praise be to Allah, a chance that will not come again.

lessons.culture: In Lebanon good news travels fast with "ألف مبروك", and whoever has it is expected to hand out sweets, so friends ask "وين الحلوينة؟". "الحمد لله", "إن شاء الله" and "بارك الله لك فيه" are said in the same words in every dialect.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "عندي خبر حلو إلك." Ask what happened, God willing it's good.
exercises.answer: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
accepted: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
خَيْر إِن شَاءَ الله، شُو صَار؟
خير إن شاء الله شو صار
kheir in shaa2 allaah, shu Saar?

too_formal.item: خيرًا إن شاء الله، ماذا حدث؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "شو صار" is the spoken "what happened".

exercises.tip: "خير إن شاء الله" hopes the news is good before hearing it.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "أخدت الوظيفة." Congratulate him and say you are very happy for him.

too_formal.item: مبروك، أنا سعيد جدًّا من أجلك
too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "مبسوطلك" is the spoken "happy for you".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "نجحت _____!" (I passed the exam!)

too_formal.feedback: This is the written preposition; in speech "في" becomes "بـ".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "مبروك، أنا كتير _____." (Congratulations, I am very happy for you, to a man.)

too_formal.feedback: This is the written way; in Beirut "happy" is "مبسوط".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "We bought a new house."

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; spoken Arabic drops the "-an" endings.

exercises.tip: "جديد" is said "jdiid", with no vowel after the ج.

exercises.prompt: Translate (to a man): "When did you hear the news?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "إيمتى" is the Lebanese "when".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Let us celebrate together this evening."

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "خلّينا" and "سوا" are the spoken "let's" and "together".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "We will have a new baby, Allah willing"?
exercises.answer: رَح يِجِينَا مَوْلُود جْدِيد إِن شَاءَ الله
accepted: رَح يِجِينَا مَوْلُود جْدِيد إِن شَاءَ الله
رح يجينا مولود جديد إن شاء الله

exercises.tip: "إن شاء الله" is always added for good things still to come.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Praise be to Allah, this is a great blessing"?
options: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; Beirut says "هيدي" for "this" (feminine).

challenge.title: Tell Me What Happened
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Lebanese conversation of at least 10 lines between two people catching up. It must include asking what happened yesterday, an answer in the past tense, a childhood memory, one thing that went wrong, and one piece of news or gossip you heard. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 16 and include both a masculine-address form and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A question about yesterday using مبارح and شو عملت or شو صار.
An answer describing something that happened, using a past-tense verb.
A memory from childhood using لمّا كنت زغير or كنّا.
Something that went wrong, using a word like خرب, ضيّعت, or تأخّرت.
A piece of news or gossip introduced with سمعت إنّو or قالولي.
At least one masculine-address form such as كنت or شفت.
At least one feminine-address form such as كنتي or شفتي.
A closing reaction such as يي, يا حرام, or الله يعينك.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: ميساء، كيفك؟ شو عملتي مبارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: Maysaa2, kiifik? shu 3milti mbeeri7?
dialogue.english: Maysa, how are you? What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: أهلين بلال، ما رح تصدّق شو صار معي مبارح!
dialogue.transliteration: ahlein Bilaal, ma ra7 teSSaddi2 shu Saar ma3i mbeeri7!
dialogue.english: Hi Bilal, you won't believe what happened to me yesterday!

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: شو في؟ قوليلي!
dialogue.transliteration: shu fii? 2uuliili!
dialogue.english: What is it? Tell me!

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: تلفوني خرب وضيّعت مفتاح البيت بنفس اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: talifuuni khirib w-Dayya3et miftaa7 el-beit b-nafs el-yoom
dialogue.english: My phone broke and I lost the house key on the same day.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: يي، يا حرام! هيك يوم بيذكّرني لمّا كنت زغير، كنا نضيّع كل شي!
dialogue.transliteration: yii, yaa 7araam! heik yoom bizakkerni lamma kent zghiir, kenna nDayyi3 kell shi!
dialogue.english: Oh no! A day like that reminds me of when I was little, we used to lose everything!

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: ههه صحيح! بس بالآخر لقيت المفتاح
dialogue.transliteration: hehe Sa7ii7! bas bil-aakher la2eit el-miftaa7
dialogue.english: Haha true! But in the end I found the key.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله. بالمناسبة، سمعت إنّو سامر خطب
dialogue.transliteration: el-7amdulillah. bel-munaasabe, sme3et 2inno Saamer khaTab
dialogue.english: Thank God. By the way, I heard Samer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: عن جدّ؟ مين قلّك؟ ما كنت أعرف!
dialogue.transliteration: 3an jadd? meen 2allak? ma kent a3ref!
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you? I didn't know!

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: قالولي الجيران، بس لسّا مش متأكد إذا صحيح
dialogue.transliteration: 2aaloolli el-jiiraan, bas lissa mish met2akked iza Sa7ii7
dialogue.english: The neighbors told me, but I'm not sure yet if it's true.

dialogue.speaker: Maysaa
dialogue.arabic: ما بعرف، عم يقولوا هيك. خلينا ننتظر ونشوف
dialogue.transliteration: ma ba3ref, 3am ye2uulu heik. khaliina nentiZer w-nshuuf
dialogue.english: I don't know, that's what they're saying. Let's wait and see.
